sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatas tāni mahārhāṇi divyāni bharatarṣabha bahūni bahurūpāṇi virajāṃsi samādade
english: Vaishampayana said: Then, O bull of the Bharatas, he gathered those many divine and most precious flowers, of many forms, pure and spotless.

sanskrit: tato vāyur mahāñ śīghro nīcaiḥ śarkarakarṣaṇaḥ prādurāsīt kharasparśaḥ saṃgrāmam abhicodayan
english: Then a great and swift wind arose, harsh to the touch, driving gravel along the ground, urging on as if stirring up a battle.

sanskrit: papāta mahatī colkā sanirghātā mahāprabhā niṣprabhaś cābhavat sūryaś channaraśmis tamovṛtaḥ
english: A great and blazing meteor fell with a thunderous crash; the sun lost its radiance, its rays covered and enveloped in darkness.

sanskrit: nirghātaś cābhavad bhīmo bhīme vikramam āsthite cacāla pṛthivī cāpi pāṃsuvarṣaṃ papāta ca
english: There was a terrible clap of thunder while Bhima was engaged in his mighty feat; the earth itself trembled, and a shower of dust fell.

sanskrit: salohitā diśaś cāsan kharavāco mṛgadvijāḥ tamovṛtam abhūt sarvaṃ na prajñāyata kiṃ cana
english: The directions turned blood-red; beasts and birds cried out harshly; everything was enveloped in darkness so that nothing could be discerned.

sanskrit: tad adbhutam abhiprekṣya dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ uvāca vadatāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ ko 'smān abhibhaviṣyati
english: Beholding that marvel, Yudhishthira, son of Dharma and foremost among the eloquent, said: "Who is it that shall overcome us?"

sanskrit: sajjībhavata bhadraṃ vaḥ pāṇḍavā yuddhadurmadāḥ yathārūpāṇi paśyāmi svabhyagro naḥ parākramaḥ
english: "Be ready, O Pandavas, intoxicated with battle — fortune attend you! By what I see, our own prowess shall prove supreme."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tato rājā vīkṣāṃ cakre samantataḥ apaśyamāno bhīmaṃ ca dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Having spoken thus, King Yudhishthira, the dharma-king, looked around in all directions, but could not see Bhima.

sanskrit: tatra kṛṣṇāṃ yamau caiva samīpasthān ariṃdamaḥ papraccha bhrātaraṃ bhīmaṃ bhīmakarmāṇam āhave
english: There the subduer of foes asked Draupadi and the twin brothers who stood nearby about his brother Bhima, terrible in battle deeds.

sanskrit: kaccin na bhīmaḥ pāñcāli kiṃ cit kṛtyaṃ cikīrṣati kṛtavān api vā vīraḥ sāhasaṃ sāhasapriyaḥ
english: "O Panchali, has Bhima not gone to do something? Or has that hero, fond of bold exploits, already performed some daring deed?"

sanskrit: ime hy akasmād utpātā mahāsamaradarśinaḥ darśayanto bhayaṃ tīvraṃ prādurbhūtāḥ samantataḥ
english: "For these sudden ill omens, portending a great battle, have manifested on all sides showing terrible fear."

sanskrit: taṃ tathā vādinaṃ kṛṣṇā pratyuvāca manasvinī priyā priyaṃ cikīrṣantī mahiṣī cāruhāsinī
english: To him speaking thus, Krishnaa — the wise one, his beloved, the beautiful-smiling queen eager to please her dear one — replied:

sanskrit: yat tat saugandhikaṃ rājann āhṛtaṃ mātariśvanā tan mayā bhīmasenasya prītayādyopapāditam
english: "O king, those Saugandhika lotuses which were brought by the wind — today I had them fetched for the delight of Bhimasena.

sanskrit: api cokto mayā vīro yadi paśyed bahūny api tāni sarvāṇy upādāya śīghram āgamyatām iti
english: "And the hero was told by me: if you find many more of them, gather them all and return quickly."

sanskrit: sa tu nūnaṃ mahābāhuḥ priyārthaṃ mama pāṇḍavaḥ prāgudīcīṃ diśaṃ rājaṃs tāny āhartum ito gataḥ
english: "He, that mighty-armed Pandava, has surely gone from here in the north-eastward direction, O king, to fetch those flowers for my sake."

sanskrit: uktas tv evaṃ tayā rājā yamāv idam athābravīt gacchāma sahitās tūrṇaṃ yena yāto vṛkodaraḥ
english: Addressed thus by her, the king then spoke to the twins: "Let us all go quickly in the direction Vrikodara has gone."

sanskrit: vahantu rākṣasā viprān yathāśrāntān yathākṛśān tvam apy amarasaṃkāśa vaha kṛṣṇāṃ ghaṭotkaca
english: "Let the rakshasas carry the brahmanas, weary and emaciated as they are; and you also, O Ghatotkacha, equal to the immortals, carry Krishnaa."

sanskrit: vyaktaṃ dūram ito bhīmaḥ praviṣṭa iti me matiḥ ciraṃ ca tasya kālo 'yaṃ sa ca vāyusamo jave
english: "It is clear to my mind that Bhima has gone deep and far from here; the time has grown long, and he is equal to the wind in speed."

sanskrit: tarasvī vainateyasya sadṛśo bhuvi laṅghane utpated api cākāśaṃ nipatec ca yathecchakam
english: "Swift, he is equal to Garuda's son in leaping on earth; he could spring up into the sky and descend again at will."

sanskrit: tam anviyāma bhavatāṃ prabhāvād rajanīcarāḥ purā sa nāparādhnoti siddhānāṃ brahmavādinām
english: "Let us follow him — by your power, O night-rangers — before he commits any offense against the Siddhas and the Brahma-speakers."

sanskrit: tathety uktvā tu te sarve haiḍimbapramukhās tadā uddeśajñāḥ kuberasya nalinyā bharatarṣabha
english: Saying "so be it," all of them, led by Hidimba's son, who knew the way to Kubera's lake, O bull of the Bharatas —

sanskrit: ādāya pāṇḍavāṃś caiva tāṃś ca viprān anekaśaḥ lomaśenaiva sahitāḥ prayayuḥ prītamānasāḥ
english: — taking up the Pandavas and those many brahmanas, together with Lomasha himself, set out with joyful hearts.

sanskrit: te gatvā sahitāḥ sarve dadṛśus tatra kānane praphullapaṅkajavatīṃ nalinīṃ sumanoharām
english: Going together, all of them saw there in the forest that charming lake adorned with fully blooming lotuses — most beautiful to behold.

sanskrit: taṃ ca bhīmaṃ mahātmānaṃ tasyās tīre vyavasthitam dadṛśur nihatāṃś caiva yakṣān suvipulekṣaṇān
english: And they saw that great-souled Bhima standing on its bank, and also saw the yakshas with large eyes, slain.

sanskrit: udyamya ca gadāṃ dorbhyāṃ nadītīre vyavasthitam prajāsaṃkṣepasamaye daṇḍahastam ivāntakam
english: He stood on the river-bank holding his mace aloft with both arms, like Death himself staff in hand at the time of universal dissolution.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā dharmarājas tu pariṣvajya punaḥ punaḥ uvāca ślakṣṇayā vācā kaunteya kim idaṃ kṛtam
english: Seeing him, the dharma-king embraced him again and again and said in gentle words: "O son of Kunti, what is this that you have done?"

sanskrit: sāhasaṃ bata bhadraṃ te devānām api cāpriyam punar evaṃ na kartavyaṃ mama ced icchasi priyam
english: "This rashness, though it may bring you glory, is displeasing even to the gods. Do not do such a thing again, if you wish to please me."

sanskrit: anuśāsya ca kaunteyaṃ padmāni pratigṛhya ca tasyām eva nalinyāṃ te vijahrur amaropamāḥ
english: Having admonished the son of Kunti and receiving the lotus flowers, they — equal to the immortals — sported together in that very lake.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu pragṛhītaśilāyudhāḥ prādurāsan mahākāyās tasyodyānasya rakṣiṇaḥ
english: At this very time there appeared the mighty-bodied guardians of that garden, armed with rocks, coming forth.

sanskrit: te dṛṣṭvā dharmarājānaṃ devarṣiṃ cāpi lomaśam nakulaṃ sahadevaṃ ca tathānyān brāhmaṇarṣabhān vinayenānatāḥ sarve praṇipetuś ca bhārata
english: Seeing the king of dharma, and the divine sage Lomasha, and Nakula and Sahadeva, and the other brahmin-seers, all of them bowed with humility and prostrated, O Bharata.

sanskrit: sāntvitā dharmarājena praseduḥ kṣaṇadācarāḥ viditāś ca kuberasya tatas te narapuṃgavāḥ ūṣur nāticiraṃ kālaṃ ramamāṇāḥ kurūdvahāḥ
english: Appeased by the dharma-king, those night-wanderers became serene; and being known to Kubera, those bull-like men, the upholders of the Kuru line, stayed there for a while, sporting in delight.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatas tān pariviśvastān vasatas tatra pāṇḍavān gateṣu teṣu rakṣaḥsu bhīmasenātmaje 'pi ca
english: Vaishampayana said: Then, while those Pandavas were living there confidently — after those rakshasas and also the son of Bhimasena had departed —

sanskrit: rahitān bhīmasenena kadā cit tān yadṛcchayā jahāra dharmarājānaṃ yamau kṛṣṇāṃ ca rākṣasaḥ
english: — left without Bhimasena, a rakshasa one day seized them by chance — the dharma-king, the twins, and Krishnaa.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇo mantrakuśalaḥ sarvāstreṣv astravittamaḥ iti bruvan pāṇḍaveyān paryupāste sma nityadā
english: Representing himself as a brahmin skilled in mantras and supremely learned in all weapons, he constantly attended upon the Pandavas daily.

sanskrit: parīkṣamāṇaḥ pārthānāṃ kalāpāni dhanūṃṣi ca antaraṃ samabhiprepsur nāmnā khyāto jaṭāsuraḥ
english: He examined the quivers and bows of the Parthas while seeking an opportunity, known by name as Jatasura.

sanskrit: sa bhīmasene niṣkrānte mṛgayārtham ariṃdame anyad rūpaṃ samāsthāya vikṛtaṃ bhairavaṃ mahat
english: When the foe-subduing Bhimasena had gone out for hunting, he assumed another form — terrible, monstrous, and enormous.

sanskrit: gṛhītvā sarvaśastrāṇi draupadīṃ parigṛhya ca prātiṣṭhata sa duṣṭātmā trīn gṛhītvā ca pāṇḍavān
english: Seizing all the weapons and taking hold of Draupadi, that evil-souled one set off, having also captured three of the Pandavas.

sanskrit: sahadevas tu yatnena tato 'pakramya pāṇḍavaḥ ākrandad bhīmasenaṃ vai yena yāto mahābalaḥ
english: But Sahadeva, the Pandava, managed to slip away with effort and cried out to Bhimasena, that mighty one, in the direction he had gone.

sanskrit: tam abravīd dharmarājo hriyamāṇo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ dharmas te hīyate mūḍha na cainaṃ samavekṣase
english: While being carried off, the dharma-king Yudhishthira spoke to him: "Your dharma declines, O fool — do you not see this at all?"

sanskrit: ye 'nye ke cin manuṣyeṣu tiryagyonigatā api gandharvayakṣarakṣāṃsi vayāṃsi paśavas tathā manuṣyān upajīvanti tatas tvam upajīvasi
english: "Whatever beings there are among humans, and even those born in animal wombs — gandharvas, yakshas, rakshasas, birds, beasts — they all live dependent upon humans; and thus do you live dependent on them."

sanskrit: samṛddhyā hy asya lokasya loko yuṣmākam ṛdhyate imaṃ ca lokaṃ śocantam anuśocanti devatāḥ pūjyamānāś ca vardhante havyakavyair yathāvidhi
english: "For by the prosperity of this world, your world too prospers; when this world grieves, the gods also grieve; and when properly worshipped, they thrive on oblations and offerings."

sanskrit: vayaṃ rāṣṭrasya goptāro rakṣitāraś ca rākṣasa rāṣṭrasyārakṣyamāṇasya kuto bhūtiḥ kutaḥ sukham
english: "We are the guardians and protectors of the kingdom, O rakshasa; for an unprotected kingdom, how can there be prosperity? How can there be happiness?"

sanskrit: na ca rājāvamantavyo rakṣasā jātv anāgasi aṇur apy apacāraś ca nāsty asmākaṃ narāśana
english: "A king who has committed no offense must never be disrespected by a rakshasa; and not even the smallest transgression exists on our part, O man-eater."

sanskrit: drogdhavyaṃ na ca mitreṣu na viśvasteṣu karhi cit yeṣāṃ cānnāni bhuñjīta yatra ca syāt pratiśrayaḥ
english: "One must never betray friends, nor those who have placed their trust; nor those whose food one has eaten, nor those who have given one shelter."

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ pratiśraye 'smākaṃ pūjyamānaḥ sukhoṣitaḥ bhuktvā cānnāni duṣprajña katham asmāñ jihīrṣasi
english: "You, who dwelt sheltered by us, were honored and lived in comfort; having eaten our food, how do you, O witless one, now seek to carry us off?"

sanskrit: evam eva vṛthācāro vṛthāvṛddho vṛthāmatiḥ vṛthāmaraṇam arhas tvaṃ vṛthādya na bhaviṣyasi
english: "Such is your character — your growth is in vain, your intelligence in vain, your conduct in vain; you deserve a vain death, and this day you shall cease to exist in vain."

sanskrit: atha ced duṣṭabuddhis tvaṃ sarvair dharmair vivarjitaḥ pradāya śastrāṇy asmākaṃ yuddhena draupadīṃ hara
english: "But if you, corrupt in mind and devoid of all dharma, wish — give back our weapons and then win Draupadi by open combat."

sanskrit: atha cet tvam avijñāya idaṃ karma kariṣyasi adharmaṃ cāpy akīrtiṃ ca loke prāpsyasi kevalam
english: "But if you do this deed without understanding, you will gain only unrighteousness and infamy in the world."

sanskrit: etām adya parāmṛśya striyaṃ rākṣasa mānuṣīm viṣam etat samāloḍya kumbhena prāśitaṃ tvayā
english: "By laying violent hands upon this woman today, O rakshasa — this human woman — it is poison you have drunk by the potful, having stirred it up yourself."

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiras tasya bhārikaḥ samapadyata sa tu bhārābhibhūtātmā na tathā śīghrago 'bhavat
english: Then Yudhishthira became a burden upon him; the rakshasa, his spirit overwhelmed by the weight, could no longer move as swiftly as before.

sanskrit: athābravīd draupadīṃ ca nakulaṃ ca yudhiṣṭhiraḥ mā bhaiṣṭa rākṣasān mūḍhād gatir asya mayā hṛtā
english: Then Yudhishthira said to Draupadi and to Nakula: "Do not fear this foolish rakshasa — I have stolen away his power of movement."

sanskrit: nātidūre mahābāhur bhavitā pavanātmajaḥ asmin muhūrte saṃprāpte na bhaviṣyati rākṣasaḥ
english: "The mighty-armed son of the wind-god will not be far away; when this moment arrives, this rakshasa shall be no more."

sanskrit: sahadevas tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā rākṣasaṃ mūḍhacetasam uvāca vacanaṃ rājan kuntīputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Sahadeva, seeing that rakshasa of dulled mind, spoke these words to king Yudhishthira, son of Kunti:

sanskrit: rājan kiṃ nāma tat kṛtyaṃ kṣatriyasyāsty ato 'dhikam yad yuddhe 'bhimukhaḥ prāṇāṃs tyajec chatrūñ jayeta vā
english: "O king, what deed is there higher for a kshatriya than this — that facing the enemy in battle he should either give up his life or conquer his foes?"

sanskrit: eṣa cāsmān vayaṃ cainaṃ yudhyamānāḥ paraṃtapa sūdayema mahābāho deśakālo hy ayaṃ nṛpa
english: "Either this one shall destroy us or we shall destroy him in battle, O scorcher of foes, O mighty-armed one — for this is the right time and place, O king."

sanskrit: kṣatradharmasya saṃprāptaḥ kālaḥ satyaparākrama jayantaḥ pātyamānā vā prāptum arhāma sadgatim
english: "The time for kshatriya dharma has arrived, O man of true valor; whether conquering or being slain, we deserve to attain the highest state."

sanskrit: rākṣase jīvamāne 'dya ravir astam iyād yadi nāhaṃ brūyāṃ punar jātu kṣatriyo 'smīti bhārata
english: "If the sun were to set today with this rakshasa still alive, I would never again say 'I am a kshatriya,' O Bharata."

sanskrit: bho bho rākṣasa tiṣṭhasva sahadevo 'smi pāṇḍavaḥ hatvā vā māṃ nayasvainān hato vādyeha svapsyasi
english: "Ho there, rakshasa — stop! I am Sahadeva, the Pandava. Either slay me and then carry them off, or lie here slain this very day."

sanskrit: tathaiva tasmin bruvati bhīmaseno yadṛcchayā prādṛśyata mahābāhuḥ savajra iva vāsavaḥ
english: Even as he was speaking thus, Bhimasena appeared by chance — mighty-armed, like Vasava armed with the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: so 'paśyad bhrātarau tatra draupadīṃ ca yaśasvinīm kṣitisthaṃ sahadevaṃ ca kṣipantaṃ rākṣasaṃ tadā
english: He saw his two brothers there, and the illustrious Draupadi, and Sahadeva on the ground hurling abuse at the rakshasa.

sanskrit: mārgāc ca rākṣasaṃ mūḍhaṃ kālopahatacetasam bhramantaṃ tatra tatraiva daivena vinivāritam
english: And he saw the foolish rakshasa, his mind stricken by fate, wandering here and there, checked and restrained by destiny.

sanskrit: bhrātṝṃs tān hriyato dṛṣṭvā draupadīṃ ca mahābalaḥ krodham āhārayad bhīmo rākṣasaṃ cedam abravīt
english: The mighty Bhima, seeing him carrying off his brothers and Draupadi, filled himself with wrath and spoke these words to the rakshasa:

sanskrit: vijñāto 'si mayā pūrvaṃ ceṣṭañ śastraparīkṣaṇe āsthā tu tvayi me nāsti yato 'si na hatas tadā brahmarūpapraticchanno na no vadasi cāpriyam
english: "You were recognized by me earlier from your behavior while inspecting the weapons; but I placed no importance on you, and so you were not killed then — for you were disguised in brahmin form and did not say anything disagreeable to us."

sanskrit: priyeṣu caramāṇaṃ tvāṃ na caivāpriyakāriṇam atithiṃ brahmarūpaṃ ca kathaṃ hanyām anāgasam rākṣasaṃ manyamāno 'pi yo hanyān narakaṃ vrajet
english: "You who moved among the beloved ones, not doing anything harmful, a guest in brahmin form — how could I slay one who had committed no offense? Even one who knew you to be a rakshasa would go to hell for killing such a one."

sanskrit: apakvasya ca kālena vadhas tava na vidyate nūnam adyāsi saṃpakvo yathā te matir īdṛśī dattā kṛṣṇāpaharaṇe kālenādbhutakarmaṇā
english: "There is no slaying by time of one who is not yet ripe; but now surely you are fully ripe, since such a resolve has been given to you by time — marvelous in its workings — to carry off Krishnaa."

sanskrit: baḍiśo 'yaṃ tvayā grastaḥ kālasūtreṇa lambitaḥ matsyo 'mbhasīva syūtāsyaḥ kathaṃ me 'dya gamiṣyasi
english: "This hook has been swallowed by you, hung on the thread of time; like a fish in water with a pierced mouth — how will you escape from me today?"

sanskrit: yaṃ cāsi prasthito deśaṃ manaḥ pūrvaṃ gataṃ ca te na taṃ gantāsi gantāsi mārgaṃ bakahiḍimbayoḥ
english: "The destination to which you set out, where your mind already went beforehand — you will not reach it; you will go the way of Baka and Hidimba."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu bhīmena rākṣasaḥ kālacoditaḥ bhīta utsṛjya tān sarvān yuddhāya samupasthitaḥ
english: Addressed thus by Bhima, the rakshasa, driven by fate, was frightened; releasing all of them, he presented himself for battle.

sanskrit: abravīc ca punar bhīmaṃ roṣāt prasphuritādharaḥ na me mūḍhā diśaḥ pāpa tvadarthaṃ me vilambanam
english: And with lips quivering from rage, he again spoke to Bhima: "My directions are not confused, O sinner — the delay was only for your sake."

sanskrit: śrutā me rākṣasā ye ye tvayā vinihatā raṇe teṣām adya kariṣyāmi tavāsreṇodakakriyām
english: "All the rakshasas I have heard of who were slain by you in battle — for them today I shall perform the water libation using your blood."

sanskrit: evam uktas tato bhīmaḥ sṛkkiṇī parisaṃlihan smayamāna iva krodhāt sākṣāt kālāntakopamaḥ bāhusaṃrambham evecchann abhidudrāva rākṣasam
english: Thus addressed, Bhima then, licking the corners of his lips, as if smiling yet burning with rage, like Death and the destroyer at the end of time in person, desiring only the fury of his arms, rushed at the rakshasa.

sanskrit: rākṣaso 'pi tadā bhīmaṃ yuddhārthinam avasthitam abhidudrāva saṃrabdho balo vajradharaṃ yathā
english: The rakshasa too rushed at Bhima who stood ready seeking battle, furious with rage, like Bali charging Indra the thunderbolt-bearer.

sanskrit: vartamāne tadā tābhyāṃ bāhuyuddhe sudāruṇe mādrīputrāv abhikruddhāv ubhāv apy abhyadhāvatām
english: While the two of them were engaged in that most terrible wrestling match, the two sons of Madri, furious, both rushed forward as well.

sanskrit: nyavārayat tau prahasan kuntīputro vṛkodaraḥ śakto 'haṃ rākṣasasyeti prekṣadhvam iti cābravīt
english: Vrikodara, son of Kunti, laughing, restrained both of them, saying: "I am capable against this rakshasa — just watch."

sanskrit: ātmanā bhrātṛbhiś cāhaṃ dharmeṇa sukṛtena ca iṣṭena ca śape rājan sūdayiṣyāmi rākṣasam
english: "By myself, by my brothers, by dharma, by my good deeds, and by my sacrifices I swear, O king, I shall destroy this rakshasa."

sanskrit: ity evam uktvā tau vīrau spardhamānau parasparam bāhubhiḥ samasajjetām ubhau rakṣovṛkodarau
english: Having spoken thus, those two heroes, competing with each other, grappled with their arms — both the rakshasa and Vrikodara.

sanskrit: tayor āsīt saṃprahāraḥ kruddhayor bhīmarakṣasoḥ amṛṣyamāṇayoḥ saṃkhye devadānavayor iva
english: There was a fierce clash between the two — the furious Bhima and the rakshasa — neither enduring the other, like gods and demons in battle.

sanskrit: ārujyārujya tau vṛkṣān anyonyam abhijaghnatuḥ jīmūtāv iva gharmānte vinadantau mahābalau
english: The two of them, uprooting tree after tree, struck each other, roaring like two storm-clouds at the end of summer — those two mighty ones.

sanskrit: babhañjatur mahāvṛkṣān ūrubhir balināṃ varau anyonyenābhisaṃrabdhau parasparajayaiṣiṇau
english: Those two best among the strong shattered great trees with their thighs, grappling with each other in fury, each seeking victory over the other.

sanskrit: tad vṛkṣayuddham abhavan mahīruhavināśanam vālisugrīvayor bhrātroḥ pureva kapisiṃhayoḥ
english: That tree-battle brought destruction to the trees, just as the battle between the brothers Vali and Sugriva, those lions among monkeys, had done before.
